description: The FGI GNSS Jamming and Spoofing Dataset Repository gathers open recordings of raw GNSS in-phase and quadrature (I/Q) samples for research on receiver resilience to jamming and spoofing, published by the Finnish Geospatial Research Institute. It has four collections on the Finnish Fairdata service: FGI-SpoofRepo, with live GPS L1 C/A, Galileo E1, GPS L5 and Galileo E5a signals under synchronous, asynchronous and meaconing spoofing (about 127 GB, 2024, described in GPS Solutions); FGI OSNMA datasets, with GPS L1 C/A and Galileo E1 signals in clean open-sky and spoofed scenarios to study Galileo navigation message authentication (about 35 GB, 2024); the FGI Jammertest 2023 repository, recorded at Andøya in Norway with a LabSat 3 wideband recorder, with one high-power jamming and two spoofing scenarios (about 152 GB, 2025); and a 2026 set of simulated recordings generated with Safran's Skydel simulator to compare the jamming resistance of low Earth orbit PNT signals with GNSS (about 124 GB). Configuration files for the FGI-GSRx software receiver are shared so the data can be processed directly. Coverage: recordings in Finland and at Andøya, Norway, plus simulated scenarios. Format and access: raw I/Q binary files and MATLAB data from Fairdata Etsin, free under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: large files; each set covers a few scenarios and receivers' behaviour differs. Simulation uses: resilience testing of positioning and timing under interference, and inputs to scenarios of GNSS loss in dependent infrastructure. Related records: Jammertest describes the Andøya trials, and FGI-GSRx processes the files.
